definitions.gloss: traditional Chinese medicine (as adapted in Japan), kampo
definitions.explanation: A system of traditional medicine based on Chinese medical principles, adapted and refined in Japan over centuries. Involves herbal remedies, acupuncture, and other treatments.

{漢方|かんぽう}⟦{医学|いがく}→医学：01301_igaku⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{体質|たいしつ}→体質：08243_taishitsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{合|あ}わせた→合わせる：01872_awaseru⟧⟦{治療|ちりょう}→治療：03503_chiryou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。

notes:
USAGE:
{漢方|かんぽう} in Japan refers specifically to the Japanese adaptation of traditional Chinese medicine, distinct from Chinese traditional medicine ({中医学|ちゅういがく}) as practiced in China. Kampo is officially recognized in Japan, and many {漢方|かんぽう}{薬|やく} are covered by health insurance.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {漢方|かんぽう}{薬|やく}: kampo medicine, herbal medicine
- {漢方|かんぽう}⟦{医学|いがく}→医学：01301_igaku⟧: kampo medical science
- {漢方|かんぽう}{医|い}: kampo practitioner
- {漢方|かんぽう}⟦{薬局|やっきょく}→薬局：01069_yakkyoku⟧: kampo pharmacy

CULTURAL NOTE:
Kampo has been practiced in Japan since the 5th-6th century. Unlike in many Western countries, kampo medicines are prescribed by mainstream doctors in Japan and are available at regular pharmacies.
